what_it_does: Before a chip is manufactured, engineers verify its design by running a software simulation of the chip's low-level blueprint (called RTL — the register-transfer level description that specifies exactly how bits move between storage elements each clock cycle). These simulations are notoriously slow, often taking days for complex processors. GSIM attacks the slowness at three nested levels: at the highest level it optimizes groups of related logic (called supernodes), at the middle level it tightens individual logic-gate operations, and at the lowest level it speeds up raw bitwise arithmetic. By combining optimizations across all three levels with efficient data structures and smarter scheduling of work, GSIM aims to make the overall simulation significantly faster.
